outcome: Causes of neonatal death (hyaline membrane disease, hypoxia, septicaemia, necrotising enterocolitis, pulmonary haemorrhage, intraventricular haemorrhage)
Maternal complications (manual removal of the placenta, ruptured uterus, anaemia with blood transfusion)
cohort: The study included 18 cases of women who underwent self-induced pregnancy termination using misoprostol after 24 weeks' gestation and were treated at a tertiary hospital in the Eastern Cape Province, South Africa between July 2011 and January 2012.
finding: Self-administration of misoprostol to induce pregnancy termination after 24 weeks' gestation contributes to preterm births and increased perinatal morbidity and mortality, alongside potential maternal complications.
followup_time: The study recorded early and late neonatal deaths, implying follow-up for at least 28 days for the live-born infants.
birth_weight: Cases included babies with birth weights ranging from <500 g to >2500 g.
gest_age: Cases included pregnancies terminated after 24 weeks' gestation.
